class_config.name: bus_peripheral
class_config.class_tree_node_basis: The registry class is a register-mapped peripheral behind a bus subordinate port; the node is 'memory-mapped, NOT a serial protocol' with a register window. The node names APB while the class also spans TL-UL / AXI-Lite / AHB / Wishbone, but the bus flavour is incidental to every floor the node carries (all of them count register-map and integration content, none of them count APB signalling), and the registry's own synonyms include apb_peripheral.
class_config.description: ORGANIC #542 — Register-mapped peripheral IP: SW-visible register map (hjson/regmap or equivalent) exposed via a bus subordinate interface (TL-UL, APB, AXI-Lite, Wishbone, AHB). No ISA / instruction-fetch semantics. L4 register map is the primary specification layer. Distinguished from bus_interconnect_protocol (wire-level protocol spec) and processor_cpu (instruction-executing). crypto_accelerator takes priority when crypto algorithm features are present. ORGANIC #677 — a MINIMAL instance (e.g. a Wishbone-mapped counter with no regmap / no test scenarios / no test cases) may honestly declare the absence via no_register_map_in_input / no_test_scenarios_in_input / no_test_cases_in_input == true; minimal_honest_absence_ok lets l_doc_structured_field_count_check waive the L4/L7/L10 typed-field floors for that honest minimal doc (NARROWER than command_protocol_applicable so a reused-IP processor_cpu still obeys its #641 populated-bring-up doctrine).
